Design (fixed before the run): compared five societies × budgets 75, 150, 300, 600, 1200, 2400, 4800, 9600 · held the same: a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.7), 12 identical agents, budget 75 split equally, no mint, no validation · measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste · 30 graphs × 5 runs on each, per row.

Caveats:

  • A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
Details

The simple model on a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, composition 0.7; level-1 ideas 3 bits long, deeper ideas every level equally hard; difficulty follows level mostly (0.8): each idea takes its own level's difficulty with chance 0.8, otherwise that of a random level); each run draws its own graph. Societies and budgets vary. Held fixed: 12 identical agents, equal money every round (f = 0), no flat mint, a knowledge reward of 1 per new bit flowing back with α, no validation.

Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
